760.text: Dimethyl glyoxime gives a red precipitate with $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$, which is used for its detection. To get this precipitate readily the best $\mathrm{pH}$ range is

Nickel(II) forms a precipitate with the organic compound dimethylglyoxime, $\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_6(\mathrm{NOH})_2$. The formation of the red chelate occurs quantitatively in a solution in which the $\mathrm{pH}$ is buffered in the range of 5 to 9 . The chelation reaction that occurs is illustrated below.
The reaction is performed in a solution buffered by either an ammonia or citrate buffer to prevent the $\mathrm{pH}$ of the solution from falling below 5 . If the $\mathrm{pH}$ does become too low the equilibrium of the above reaction favors the formation of nickel(II) ion, causing the dissolution of $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{DMG})_2$ back into the mother liquor.

1678.subject: Physics
1678.text: A man is at a distance of $6 \mathrm{~m}$ from a bus. The bus begins to move with a constant acceleration of $3 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$. In order to catch the bus, the minimum speed with which the man should run towards the bus is
1678.sol:
If the man did not run, the bus would be at a distance $s_1$ at time $t$ given by
$s_1=6+\frac{1}{2} a t^2=6+\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times t^2=6+\frac{3}{2} t^2$
If $v$ is the speed of man, he would cover a distance $s_2=v t$ in time $t$. To catch the bus, $s_1=s_2$
$6+\frac{3}{2} t^2=v t \quad$ or $\quad t^2-\frac{2 v}{3} t+4=0$
which gives $t=\frac{2 v}{6} \pm \frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{4 v^2}{9}-16\right]^{1 / 2}$
Now, $t$ will be real if $\left(\frac{4 v^2}{9}-16\right)$ is positive or zero. Minimum $v$ corresponds to $\frac{4 v^2}{9}-16=0$ which gives $v=6 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$.

2100.subject: Zoology
2100.text: Which one of the following events is correctly matched with the time period in a normal menstrual cycle?
options: Endometrium secretes nutrients for implantation : 11-18 days
2100.sol:
Menstruation is a part of the female reproductive cycle that starts when girls become sexually mature at the time of puberty. The parts of the body involved in the menstrual cycle include the brain, pituitary gland, uterus and cervix, ovaries, fallopian tubes and vagina. The following events given in the options occur in a normal menstrual cycle.
(i) Release of egg called ovulation usually takes place roughly 14 days after the first day of the start of a period for fertilization.
(ii) Following menstruation endometrium regenerates about 8 days during the proliferative phase.
(iii) Implantation occurs after 7 days of fertilization.
(iv) Progesterone level rises after ovulation which occurs after 14 days.

3317.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3317.text: Arrange N, S, O and F in order of decreasing electron gain enthalpy.
3317.sol:
Electron gain enthalpy increases with decrease in atomic size. On moving from left to right in the periodic table, the atomic size decreases and electron gain enthalpy increase for fluorine.
In case of oxygen, due to its small size and compact nature, the incoming electron is not accomodated with ease resulting into low electron gain enthalpy than sulphur. So the correct order of electron gain enthalpy is $\mathrm{F} > \mathrm{S} > \mathrm{O} > \mathrm{N}$.

6170.text: If the straight line $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = p$ touches the curve $\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)n +   \left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)$n = 2at the $point  \left(a, b\right) on it and \dfrac{1}{a2} + \dfrac{1}{b2} = \dfrac{k}{p2} t$hen $k =$
6170.sol:
The line $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = p$ is a tangent to 

${\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{n} + {\left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)}^{n} = 2$ at $\left(a, b\right)$.

Differentiating ${\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{n} + {\left(\dfrac{y}{b}\right)}^{n} = 2$, we get

$\dfrac{n}{{a}^{n}}{\left(x\right)}^{n - 1} + \dfrac{n}{{b}^{n}}{\left(y\right)}^{n - 1}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

i.e. ${\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)}_{\left(a, b\right)} = - \dfrac{b}{a}$

Now equation of tangent at $\left(a, b\right)$ will be

$y - b = - \dfrac{b}{a}\left(x - a\right) ⇒ ay - ab = - bx + ab$

$⇒ bx + ay = 2ab$

Comparing with $xcos\alpha + ysin\alpha = p$, we get

$cos\alpha = b, sin\alpha = a, p = 2ab$

i.e. $\dfrac{1}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{b}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{{cos}^{2}\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{{sin}^{2}\alpha} = \dfrac{1}{{sin}^{2}\alpha{cos}^{2}\alpha}$

Also, $\dfrac{k}{{p}^{2}} = \dfrac{k}{4{a}^{2}{b}^{2}} = \dfrac{k}{4{sin}^{2}\alpha{cos}^{2}\alpha}$

Hence, $k = 4$

20132.text:
The variation of the molar conductivity with concentration of an electrolyte $(X)$ in aqueous solution is shown in the given figure.
The electrolyte ' X ' is:
20132.sol:
The graph shows the variation of molar conductivity (\lambda_m$) with the square root of concentration (\sqrt{c}$).

For strong electrolytes like $\text{NaCl}$, $\text{KCl}$, and $\text{HNO}_3$, the molar conductivity increases linearly with decreasing concentration according to the Kohlrausch equation: $\lambda_m = \lambda_m^0 - A\sqrt{c}$. These electrolytes show a gradual increase in $\lambda_m$ as concentration decreases, and they can be extrapolated to infinite dilution to find $\lambda_m^0$.

For weak electrolytes like $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, the molar conductivity increases sharply as the concentration decreases, especially at very low concentrations. This is due to the increase in the degree of dissociation of the weak electrolyte as the solution is diluted. The curve for a weak electrolyte does not show a linear relationship with $\sqrt{c} and cannot be extrapolated to infinite dilution to determine \lambda_m^0$.

The provided graph exhibits a sharp increase in $\lambda_m$ as $\sqrt{c} approaches zero, which is characteristic of a weak electrolyte. Among the given options, \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ is the only weak electrolyte.

Answer: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$

20795.text: $\textO^{2-}$, $\text{F}^-$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Al}^{3+}$, $\text{O}_2$, $\text{F}_2$. How many of the species given above are isoelectronic?
20795.sol:
Isoelectronic species have the same number of electrons.

$O^{2-}$: $8 + 2 = 10$ electrons
$F^-$: $9 + 1 = 10$ electrons
$Mg^{2+}$: $12 - 2 = 10$ electrons
$Al^{3+}$: $13 - 3 = 10$ electrons
$O_2$: $2 \times 8 = 16$ electrons
$F_2$: $2 \times 9 = 18$ electrons

$O^{2-}$, $F^-$, $Mg^{2+}$, and $Al^{3+}$ all have 10 electrons. Thus 4 species are isoelectronic.

20930.text: A spherical snowball is melting such that its volume is decreasing at the rate of $1 \mathrm{ cm}^3 / \mathrm\min$. The rate at which the diameter is decreasing when the diameter is 10 cm is
20930.sol:
Let $V$ be the volume and $D$ be the diameter of the spherical snowball. The volume of a sphere is given by $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^3$, where $r$ is the radius. Since $D = 2r$, we have $r = \dfrac{D}{2}$.

Substituting $r$ in terms of $D$, $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi \left( \dfrac{D}{2} \right)^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi \dfrac{D^3}{8} = \dfrac{\pi D^3}{6}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{6} \times 3D^2 \dfrac{dD}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{2} \dfrac{dD}{dt}$.

Given that the volume is decreasing at a rate of $1 \text{ cm}^3/\text\min$, we have $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -1$. We want to find the rate at which the diameter is decreasing, which is $-\dfrac{dD}{dt}$ when $D = 10 \text{ cm}$.

Substituting the values into the derivative equation: $-1 = \dfrac{\pi (10)^2}{2} \dfrac{dD}{dt} = \dfrac{100 \pi}{2} \dfrac{dD}{dt} = 50 \pi \dfrac{dD}{dt}$.

Solving for $\dfrac{dD}{dt}$, we get $\dfrac{dD}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{50 \pi}$.

The rate at which the diameter is decreasing is $-\dfrac{dD}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{50 \pi} \text{ cm/min}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{50 \pi} \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm\min$

21350.text: The particular solution of $e^{\dfrac{d y}{d x}}=2 x+1$ given that $y=1$ when $x=0$ is
21350.sol:
Given the differential equation $e^{\dfrac{dy}{dx}} = 2x + 1$.

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides, we get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \ln(2x + 1)$.

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we have $y = \int \ln(2x + 1) dx$.

Let $u = 2x + 1$, then $du = 2 dx$, which implies $dx = \dfrac{1}{2} du$.

Substituting these into the integral, $y = \dfrac{1}{2} \int \ln(u) du$.

Using integration by parts, $\int \ln(u) du = u \ln(u) - u + C$.

Thus, $y = \dfrac{1}{2} (u \ln(u) - u) + C = \dfrac{1}{2} ((2x + 1) \ln(2x + 1) - (2x + 1)) + C$.

$y = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \ln(2x + 1) - x - \dfrac{1}{2} + C$.

Given $y = 1$ when $x = 0$, substituting these values: $1 = \left(0 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \ln(1) - 0 - \dfrac{1}{2} + C$.

$1 = 0 - 0 - \dfrac{1}{2} + C$, which gives $C = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

Substituting $C$ back into the equation: $y = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \ln(2x + 1) - x - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{2} = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \ln(2x + 1) - x + 1$.

Answer: $y=\left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \log |2 x+1|-x+1$

22297.text:
The scalar product of the vector $\vec{a}=\hat{\imath}+\hat{\jmath}+\hat{k}$ with a unit vector along the sum of the vectors $\vec{b}=2 \hat{\imath}+4 \hat{\jmath}-\lambda \hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}=\hat{\imath}+2 \hat{\jmath}+3 \hat{k}$ is equal to one.
Then the value of ' $\lambda$ ' is
22297.sol:
Given $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - \lambda\hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$.

Calculate the sum vector $\vec{d} = \vec{b} + \vec{c} = (2+1)\hat{i} + (4+2)\hat{j} + (3-\lambda)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + (3-\lambda)\hat{k}$.

The unit vector along $\vec{d}$ is $\hat{d} = \dfrac{\vec{d}}{|\vec{d}|} = \dfrac{3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + (3-\lambda)\hat{k}}{\sqrt{3^2 + 6^2 + (3-\lambda)^2}}$.

The scalar product $\vec{a} \cdot \hat{d} = 1$ implies $\dfrac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d}}{|\vec{d}|} = 1$, so $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d} = |\vec{d}|$.

Calculate $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d} = (1)(3) + (1)(6) + (1)(3-\lambda) = 3 + 6 + 3 - \lambda = 12 - \lambda$.

Calculate $|\vec{d}| = \sqrt{9 + 36 + (3-\lambda)^2} = \sqrt{45 + (3-\lambda)^2}$.

Equating the two: $12 - \lambda = \sqrt{45 + 9 - 6\lambda + \lambda^2} = \sqrt{54 - 6\lambda + \lambda^2}$.

Squaring both sides: $(12 - \lambda)^2 = 54 - 6\lambda + \lambda^2$.

$144 - 24\lambda + \lambda^2 = 54 - 6\lambda + \lambda^2$.

$144 - 54 = 24\lambda - 6\lambda$.

$90 = 18\lambda$.

$\lambda = \dfrac{90}{18} = 5$.

Answer: 5

22604.subject: Physics
22604.text: Figure below shows a network of resistors, cells, and a capacitor at steady state. What is the current through the resistance 4 $\Omega$ ?
22604.sol:
At steady state, capacitor acts as open circuit \Rightarrow no current through $3\mu F$ branch and the $2\Omega$ top-left resistor.

Simplified circuit has two active branches. Let left node be $V_A$, right node = 0 V (ground). The 6 V cell sets the middle wire at +6 V.

Current through middle branch (via 2 V cell and $1\Omega$):
$I_1 = \dfrac{(V_A + 2) - 6}{1} = V_A - 4$

Current through bottom branch (via 3 V cell and $4\Omega$):
$I_2 = \dfrac{(V_A - 3) - 0}{4} = \dfrac{V_A - 3}{4}$

KCL at node A: $(V_A - 4) + \dfrac{V_A - 3}{4} = 0$

$4V_A - 16 + V_A - 3 = 0 \Rightarrow 5V_A = 19 \Rightarrow V_A = 3.8$ V

$I_{4\Omega} = \dfrac{3.8 - 3}{4} = \dfrac{0.8}{4} = 0.2$ A

22974.subject: Physics
22974.text: Action and reaction can never balance out because
options: They are equal in magnitude but not opposite always.
They are unequal in magnitudes even though opposite in direction
Though they are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction they act on different bodies.
22974.sol:
According to Newton's third law of motion, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

These two forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

However, the fundamental reason they do not balance each other out is that they act on two different bodies. Since the forces are applied to different objects, they cannot result in the net force on a single body being zero.

Answer: Though they are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction they act on different bodies.

23461.subject: Physics
23461.text:
Which of the following is incorrect?
A. Fermi level is the energy possessed by an electron at zero kelvin.
B. Fermi level for an extrinsic semiconductor lies towards the conduction band for n-type semiconductor
C. Fermi level for an extrinsic semiconductor lies towards the valence band for p-type semiconductor
D. Fermi level is the energy possessed by an electron at zero degree Celsius.
23461.sol:
The Fermi level is defined as the highest energy state occupied by electrons in a system at absolute zero temperature, which is $0$ Kelvin. Statement A describes this definition correctly.

In an n-type semiconductor, the addition of donor impurities introduces energy levels just below the conduction band, causing the Fermi level to shift upwards towards the conduction band. Statement B is correct.

In a p-type semiconductor, the addition of acceptor impurities introduces energy levels just above the valence band, causing the Fermi level to shift downwards towards the valence band. Statement C is correct.

Statement D claims the Fermi level is the energy possessed by an electron at $0$ degree Celsius ($273.15$ K). This is incorrect because the definition of the Fermi level is strictly tied to absolute zero ($0$ K).

Answer: D

The plot given below shows $P - T$ curves (where, $P$ is the pressure and $T$ is the temperature) for two solvents $X$ and $Y$ and isomolal solutions of $NaCl$ in these solvents. $NaCl$ is completely dissociates in both the solvents.

From the graph:
For the solvent $X$,    

$∆ {\text{T}}_{bx} = 2$
$∆ {\text{T}}_{bx} = {m}_{NaCl} \times {K}_{b\left(x\right)} . . . \left(i\right)$
For the solvent $Y$,   

$∆ {\text{T}}_{by} = 1$
$∆ {\text{T}}_{b\left(y\right)} = {m}_{NaCl} \times {K}_{b\left(y\right)} . . . \left(ii\right)$
From the equations ($i$) and ($ii$),
$⇒ \dfrac{{K}_{b\left(x\right)}}{{K}_{b\left(y\right)}} = 2$
For the solute $S$,

$i = \left(1 - \dfrac{\text{\alpha}}{2}\right)$
$∆ {\text{T}}_{b\left(x\right)\left(s\right)} = \left(1 - \dfrac{{\text{\alpha}}_{1}}{2}\right){K}_{b\left(x\right)}$
$∆ {\text{T}}_{b\left(y\right)\left(s\right)} = \left(1 - \dfrac{{\text{\alpha}}_{2}}{2}\right){K}_{b\left(y\right)}$
Given: 

$∆ {\text{T}}_{b\left(x\right)\left(s\right)} = 3 ∆ {\text{T}}_{b\left(y\right)\left(s\right)}$
$\left(1 - \dfrac{{\text{\alpha}}_{1}}{2}\right){K}_{b\left(x\right)} = 3 \times \left(1 - \dfrac{{\text{\alpha}}_{1}}{2}\right) \times {k}_{b\left(y\right)}$
$2\left(1 - \dfrac{{\text{\alpha}}_{1}}{2}\right) = 3\left(1 - \dfrac{{\text{\alpha}}_{2}}{2}\right)$
${\text{\alpha}}_{2} = 0 .7$
So, $\text{\alpha} = 0 .05$

Six cards and six envelopes are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and cards are to be placed in envelopes so that

So the required number of ways when card 1 is placed in the envelope numbered 2 = 265 / 5 = 53

26874.subject: Chemistry
26874.text:
Number of compounds from the following which will not produce orange red precipitate with Benedict solution is........
Glucose, maltose, sucrose, ribose,$2$-deoxyribose, amylose, lactose
26874.sol:
Except sucrose and amylose all others, give orange red precipitate with Benedict solution.
Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose. It does not have a free aldehyde or ketone group and, therefore, cannot undergo oxidation and reduce the Benedict's reagent. As a result, sucrose will not produce an orange-red precipitate with the Benedict's solution.

Amylose is a polysaccharide composed of multiple glucose units linked together. While glucose, a monosaccharide, is a reducing sugar, the glycosidic bonds in amylose prevent the free aldehyde or ketone group from being available for oxidation. As a result, amylose, as a part of starch, does not give a positive Benedict's test and will not produce an orange-red precipitate.

Match List I with List I

A. Ziegler catalyst I. Rhodium
B. Blood Pigment II. Cobalt
C. Wilkinson catalyst III. Iron

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
27467.sol:
Ziegler catalyst $\to$ Titanium

Ziegler- Natta catalyst contains two parts – a transition metal compound and an organoaluminum compound.  Organoaluminum compounds contain bonds between aluminum and carbon atoms. Examples of Ziegler-Natta catalysts include ${TiCl}_{4} + {Et}_{3}Al and {TiCl}_{3} + {AlEt}_{2}Cl$. So, if we want to write the chemical formula of one of the Ziegler-Natta catalysts then it can be represented as ${TiCl}_{4}Al ( {CH}_{3}{)}_{2} ( {CH}_{2}{)}_{2}Cl$.

Blood pigment $\to$Iron

Haemoglobin: RBCs/erythrocytes play an important role in the transport of oxygen to various tissues. It is mainly due to the presence of an iron-containing, red-colored pigment called haemoglobin. The presence of haemoglobin gives RBCs the red colour.

Wilkinson catalyst$\to$Rhodium

Wilkinson's catalyst is usually obtained by treating rhodium$\left(III\right)$ chloride hydrate with an excess of triphenylphosphine in refluxing ethanol. Triphenylphosphine serves as both a ligand and a two-electron reducing agent that oxidises itself from oxidation state $\left(III\right)$ to$\left(V\right)$.

Vitamin ${B}_{12} \to$Cobalt

Cobalt is a major part of the structure of vitamin $B12$. Therefore, if you get enough vitamin $B12$, you will also get enough cobalt. Adults need about $0 . 0015mg$ ($1 . 5$ micrograms) of vitamin $B12$ a day.

27695.subject: Chemistry
27695.text: Bromine trifluoride autoionizes to form $\text{BrF}_2^{\oplus}$ and $\text{BrF}_4^{\ominus}$. The shapes of the cation and anion are respectively ________, and ________.
27695.sol:
The autoionization of bromine trifluoride is given by the reaction:

$2\text{BrF}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{BrF}_2^{\oplus} + \text{BrF}_4^{\ominus}$

For the cation $\text{BrF}_2^{\oplus}$:
The central atom Br has $7$ valence electrons. Due to the positive charge, it has $7 - 1 = 6$ electrons available.
It forms $2$ single bonds with F atoms, leaving $4$ electrons, which constitute $2$ lone pairs.
Steric number = $2$ (bond pairs) + $2$ (lone pairs) = $4$.
The hybridization is $sp^3$. With $2$ bond pairs and $2$ lone pairs, the shape is bent (or V-shaped).

For the anion $\text{BrF}_4^{\ominus}$:
The central atom Br has $7$ valence electrons. Due to the negative charge, it has $7 + 1 = 8$ electrons available.
It forms $4$ single bonds with F atoms, leaving $4$ electrons, which constitute $2$ lone pairs.
Steric number = $4$ (bond pairs) + $2$ (lone pairs) = $6$.
The hybridization is $sp^3d^2$. To minimize repulsion, the $2$ lone pairs occupy opposite (trans) positions in the octahedral geometry, resulting in a square planar shape.

Thus, the shapes of the cation and anion are bent and square planar, respectively.

Answer: bent, square planar

28132.subject: Chemistry
28132.text:
Given below are two statements:
$R=8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ and $1$ cal $=4.2$ J
Statement I: When $E_a=12.6$ kcal/mol, the room temperature rate constant is doubled by a $10\,^\circ$C increase in temperature ($298$ K to $308$ K)
Statement II: For a first order reactions A $\rightarrow$ B,

Here $[A]_o$ is the initial concentration of A and $t_{1/2}$ is half life of reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
28132.sol:
For Statement I:
According to the Arrhenius equation:
$\log \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)$

Given that the rate constant doubles, $k_2 = 2k_1$. The temperatures are $T_1 = 298$ K and $T_2 = 308$ K.
The gas constant $R = 8.314$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1} = \dfrac{8.314}{4.2}$ cal K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1} \approx 1.98$ cal K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$.

Substituting the values:
$\log(2) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \times 1.98} \left( \dfrac{308 - 298}{298 \times 308} \right)$

$0.301 = \dfrac{E_a}{4.56} \left( \dfrac{10}{91784} \right)$

$E_a = \dfrac{0.301 \times 4.56 \times 91784}{10} \approx 12598$ cal/mol $\approx 12.6$ kcal/mol.
Thus, Statement I is true.

For Statement II:
For a first order reaction, the half-life is given by:
$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$
This indicates that the half-life of a first order reaction is independent of the initial concentration $[A]_o$. The graph of $t_{1/2}$ versus $[A]_o$ should be a horizontal line parallel to the concentration axis.
The given graph shows $t_{1/2}$ directly proportional to $[A]_o$, which corresponds to a zero order reaction ($t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_o}{2k}$).
Thus, Statement II is false.

Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

31429.text:
Match List I with List II
(A) Slaked lime (I) $NaOH$
(B) Dead burnt plaster (II) $Ca ( OH{)}_{2}$
(C) Caustic soda (III) ${Na}_{2}{CO}_{3} \cdot 10{H}_{2}O$
(D) Washing soda (IV) ${CaSO}_{4}$
Choose the correct answer form the options given below:
31429.sol:
(A) Slaked lime: Calcium oxide is a white amorphous solid. It has a melting point of 2870 K. On exposure to the atmosphere, it absorbs moisture and carbon dioxide.

$CaO + {H}_{2}O \to Ca ( OH{)}_{2}$

$CaO + {CO}_{2} \to {CaCO}_{3}$

The addition of a limited amount of water breaks the lump of lime. This process is called slaking of lime.

(B) Dead burnt plaster: Calcium sulphate is a hemihydrate of calcium sulphate. It is obtained when gypsum, ${CaSO}_{4} . 2{H}_{2}O$ is heated at 393K.

$2 ( {CaSO}_{4} . 2{H}_{2}O ) \to 2 ( {CaSO}_{4} ) . {H}_{2}O + 3{H}_{2}O$

Above 393 K, no water of crystallisation is left and anhydrous calcium sulphate, ${CaSO}_{4}$ is formed. This is known as ‘dead burnt plaster’.

(C) Caustic soda: Sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) $NaOH$ is generally prepared commercially by the electrolysis of sodium chloride in Castner-Kellner cell. A brine solution is electrolysed using a mercury cathode and a carbon anode. Sodium metal discharged at the cathode combines with mercury to form sodium amalgam.

(D) Washing soda: Sodium carbonate is a white crystalline solid which exists as a decahydrate, ${Na}_{2}{CO}_{3} . 10{H}_{2}O$. This is also called washing soda. It is readily soluble in water.

So, the correct matching is (A)-II, (B)-IV, (C)-I, (D)-III.

37015.text: The sum of the first ten terms of an A.P. is $160$ and the sum of the first two terms of a G.P. is $8$. If the first term of the A.P. is equal to the common ratio of the G.P. and the first term of the G.P. is equal to common difference of the A.P., then the sum of all possible values of the first term of the G.P. is:
37015.sol:
Let the first term of the A.P. be $a$ and its common difference be $d$.
Let the first term of the G.P. be $A$ and its common ratio be $R$.

Given that the sum of the first ten terms of the A.P. is $160$:
$\dfrac{10}{2} [2a + (10 - 1)d] = 160$
$5(2a + 9d) = 160$
$2a + 9d = 32$

Given that the sum of the first two terms of the G.P. is $8$:
$A + AR = 8$
$A(1 + R) = 8$

We are also given that $a = R$ and $A = d$. Substituting these into the first equation:
$2R + 9A = 32$
$R = \dfrac{32 - 9A}{2}$

Substitute $R$ into the second equation:
$A \left(1 + \dfrac{32 - 9A}{2}\right) = 8$
$A \left(\dfrac{2 + 32 - 9A}{2}\right) = 8$
$A(34 - 9A) = 16$
$34A - 9A^2 = 16$
$9A^2 - 34A + 16 = 0$

This is a quadratic equation in $A$. The discriminant is $\Delta = (-34)^2 - 4(9)(16) = 1156 - 576 = 580 > 0$, so there are two distinct real values for $A$.

The sum of all possible values of the first term of the G.P. ($A$) is the sum of the roots of this quadratic equation:
Sum of roots $= -\dfrac{\text{coefficient of } A}{\text{coefficient of } A^2} = \dfrac{34}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{34}{9}$

37134.sol:
Given, $\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{2{n}^{2} + 3n + 4}{( 2n ) !}$

$\dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{2n ( 2n - 1 ) + 8n + 8}{( 2n ) !}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{( 2n - 2 ) !} + 2\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{( 2n - 1 ) !} + 4\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{( 2n ) !} . . . . ( 1 )$

We know the expansion of exponential functions as,

${e}^{x} = 1 + \dfrac{x}{1 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3 !} + \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4 !} + \ldots \ldots \infty$

$e = 1 + 1 + \dfrac{1}{2 !} + \dfrac{1}{3 !} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} + \ldots \ldots \infty = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{r !}$

${e}^{- 1} = 1 - 1 + \dfrac{1}{2 !} - \dfrac{1}{3 !} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} + \ldots \ldots \infty = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{\infty}\dfrac{{\left(- 1\right)}^{r}}{r !}$

$\left(e + \dfrac{1}{e}\right) = 2\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2 !} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} + \ldots \ldots .\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{\left(\text{even}\right) !}\right)$

$e - \dfrac{1}{e} = \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{3 !} + \dfrac{1}{5 !} + \ldots . .\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{\left(\text{odd}\right) !}\right)$

Now from equation $\left(1\right)$,

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{( 2n - 2 ) !}\right) + 2\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{( 2n - 1 ) !} + 4\mathop{∑}_{n = 1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{( 2n ) !}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{e + \dfrac{1}{e}}{2}\right] + 2\left[\dfrac{e - \dfrac{1}{e}}{2}\right] + 4\left(\dfrac{e + \dfrac{1}{e} - 2}{2}\right)$

$= \dfrac{\left(e + \dfrac{1}{e}\right)}{4} + e - \dfrac{1}{e} + 2e + \dfrac{2}{e} - 4$

$= \dfrac{13}{4}e + \dfrac{5}{4e} - 4$

37885.text: The shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r}=\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\dfrac{8}{3}\hat{k}\right)+\lambda(2\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+6\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\hat{i}-\dfrac{1}{3}\hat{k}\right)+\mu(\hat{j}-\hat{k})$, $\lambda,\mu \in \mathbb{R}$, is:
37885.sol:
The given lines are $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_1 + \lambda \vec{b}_1$ and $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_2 + \mu \vec{b}_2$, where:

$\vec{a}_1 = \dfrac{1}{3}\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \dfrac{8}{3}\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}_1 = 2\hat{i} - 5\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$

$\vec{a}_2 = -\dfrac{2}{3}\hat{i} - \dfrac{1}{3}\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}_2 = \hat{j} - \hat{k}$

The shortest distance between two skew lines is given by $d = \dfrac{|(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)|}{|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2|}$.

First, finding the vector $\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1$:

$\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1 = \left(-\dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\hat{i} + (0 - 2)\hat{j} + \left(-\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\hat{k} = -\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

Next, finding the cross product $\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2$:

$\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(5 - 6) - \hat{j}(-2 - 0) + \hat{k}(2 - 0) = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

The magnitude of the cross product is:

$|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = 3$

Now, finding the dot product $(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)$:

$(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) = (-\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}) \cdot (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$

$= (-1)(-1) + (-2)(2) + (-3)(2) = 1 - 4 - 6 = -9$

Finally, the shortest distance is:

$d = \dfrac{|-9|}{3} = \dfrac{9}{3} = 3$

Answer: $3$

38940.text: Angular momentum of an electron in a hydrogen atom is $\dfrac{3h}{\pi}$, then the energy of the electron is _______ eV.
38940.sol:
The angular momentum of an electron in the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by Bohr's quantization rule:

$L = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$

Given that the angular momentum is $\dfrac{3h}{\pi}$, we can equate the two expressions:

$\dfrac{nh}{2\pi} = \dfrac{3h}{\pi}$

Solving for $n$, we get:

$n = 6$

The energy of an electron in the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by the formula:

$E_n = -\dfrac{13.6}{n^2} \text{ eV}$

Substituting $n = 6$ into the energy formula:

$E_6 = -\dfrac{13.6}{6^2} \text{ eV}$

$E_6 = -\dfrac{13.6}{36} \text{ eV}$

$E_6 \approx -0.377 \text{ eV} \approx -0.38 \text{ eV}$

Answer: $-0.38$

42251.subject: Physics
42251.text: A juggler throws balls vertically upwards with same initial velocity in air. When the first ball reaches its highest position, he throws the next ball. Assuming the juggler throws $n$ balls per second, the maximum height the balls can reach is
42251.sol:
As the juggler is throwing $n$ balls each second and ${2}^{nd}$ when the first is at its highest point, so the time taken by one ball to reach the highest point, $t = \dfrac{1}{n}s$.

And as at highest point $v = 0$.

So, from first equation of motion,

$v = u + at ⇒ 0 = u - g\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right) ⇒ u = \dfrac{g}{n}$

Now in order to calculate height, using second equation of motion, we have:
$\text{S} = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}{\text{at}}^{2}$ ...(i)

$⇒ h = \dfrac{1}{n} \times \dfrac{g}{n} - \dfrac{1}{2}\text{g} \times {\left(\dfrac{1}{n}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{g}{2{n}^{2}}$

So, the balls rise up to a height of $h = \dfrac{g}{2{n}^{2}}m$.

From \left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right),

$2a $\left(27\right)$ = 9 $\left(2a{s}^{'}\right)$

$⇒ {s}^{'} = 3m$

Heat absorbed by water: $Q = mc\Delta T = 4 \times 4200 \times 16 = 268800$ J.
Volume change: $V_1 = 4/1000 = 0.004$ m³ at 4°C, $V_2 = 4/998 ≈ 0.00401$ m³ at 20°C.
Work done by water at constant pressure: $W = P_{atm}\Delta V = 10^5 \times 0.00001 = 0.8$ J.
By first law of thermodynamics: $\Delta U = Q - W = 268800 - 0.8 = 268799.2$ J

45803.subject: Chemistry
45803.text: Choose the incorrect statement about noble gas?
options: Boiling point increases with increasing atomic mass
Helium has least tendency to form compound
Noble gases have some value of electron affinity
Xenon has maximum number of compounds
45803.sol:
(1) Intermolecular van der Waals' force exists between atoms of noble gases. The magnitude of these forces increases with increasing atomic mass which directly related to boiling point.
(2) As ionisation energy of helium is maximum, thus, electrons are lightly held to the nucleus and therefore has least tendency to form compound.
(3) As valence shells of noble gases are complete, thus they do not show tendency to gain electrons. Therefore, they have zero electron affinity.
(4) As Xenon has lowest ionisation energy, they have maximum number of compounds.

47280.subject: Biology
47280.text:
Observe the flowchart with reference to joints and their examples.

Choose the correct option that matches with the letters given in the boxes.
options: A - Cartilaginous joint, B - Pivot joint, C - Knee joint, D - Cranial sutures
A - Pivot joint, B - Knee joint, C - Cranial sutures, D - Cartilaginous joint
A - Saddle joint, B - Cranial sutures, C - Cartilaginous joint, D - Pivot joint
A - Cranial sutures, B - Cartilaginous joint, C - Pivot joint, D - Knee joint
47280.sol:
Based on the classification of joints in the human body:

1. Joints are primarily classified into three structural types: Fibrous, Cartilaginous, and Synovial.
2. Fibrous joints do not allow any movement. An example of this is the flat skull bones which fuse end-to-end with the help of dense fibrous connective tissues to form Cranial sutures. Thus, A represents Cranial sutures.
3. The joint between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column is a Cartilaginous joint, which permits limited movement. Thus, B represents Cartilaginous joint.
4. Synovial joints allow considerable movement. The joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae is a Pivot joint. Thus, C represents Pivot joint.
5. A Hinge joint allows movement primarily in one plane. A common example is the Knee joint (or elbow joint). Thus, D represents Knee joint.

Matching these with the given options, we get:
A - Cranial sutures
B - Cartilaginous joint
C - Pivot joint
D - Knee joint

Answer: A - Cranial sutures, B - Cartilaginous joint, C - Pivot joint, D - Knee joint

49465.text: If $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, \ldots, 10\}$, then the number of non-empty subsets of A containing only even number is
49465.sol:
Given set $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4, \ldots, 10\}$.

The subsets must contain only even numbers. The even numbers in set $A$ are $2, 4, 6, 8, 10$.

Let $E$ be the set of even numbers in $A$, so $E = \{2, 4, 6, 8, 10\}$.

The number of elements in $E$ is $n(E) = 5$.

The total number of subsets of $E$ is $2^5 = 32$.

Since we need the number of non-empty subsets, we subtract the empty set.

The number of non-empty subsets of $E$ is $2^5 - 1 = 32 - 1 = 31$.

Answer: $31$

51984.subject: Mathematics
51984.text: The number of solutions to $sin\left(\pi\sin^{2}\theta\right) + sin \left(\pi\cos^{2}\theta\right) =2cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}}}{2}cos\theta\right) satisfying $0 $\le \theta \lle2\pi$ is
51984.sol:
The given equation 

$sin\left(\pi{sin}^{2}\theta\right) + sin\left(\pi{cos}^{2}\theta\right) = 2cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}cos\theta\right)$

$⇒ 2sin\left(\dfrac{\pi\left({sin}^{2}\theta + {cos}^{2}\theta\right)}{2}\right)$

$cos\left(\dfrac{\pi\left({sin}^{2}\theta - {cos}^{2}\theta\right)}{2}\right) = 2cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}cos\theta\right)$

$⇒ cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}cos2\theta\right) = cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}cos\theta\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{2}cos2\theta = 2n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{2}cos\theta$, $n \in$ Integers

$⇒ cos2\theta = 4n \pm cos\theta, n \in I$.

Case $I$

If $cos2\theta = 4n + cos\theta ⇒ cos2\theta - cos\theta = 4n$

The above equation will hold only if $n = 0$, 

so $cos2\theta = cos\theta$

$⇒ 2{cos}^{2}\theta - cos\theta - 1 = 0 ⇒ cos\theta = 1, - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = 2k\pi, 2k\pi \pm \dfrac{2\pi}{3}, k \in I$

$∵ \theta \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]$

So, $\theta = 0, 2\pi, \dfrac{2\pi}{3}, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}$

Case $II$

If $cos2\theta = 4n - cos\theta$

$⇒ cos2\theta + cos\theta = 4n$

The above equation will hold only if $n = 0$,

so $cos2\theta + cos\theta = 0$

$⇒ 2{cos}^{2}\theta + cos\theta - 1 = 0$

$⇒ cos\theta = - 1, \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \theta = \left(2m + 1\right)\pi, 2m\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3}, m \in I$.

$∵ \theta \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]$

So, $\theta = \pi, \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3}$

$∴$ There are total $7$ solutions.

57799.subject: Chemistry
57799.text: Propene on hydroboration followed by oxidation with alkaline peroxide forms.
57799.sol:
Hydroboration-oxidation of propene proceeds through anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond.

The reaction begins with hydroboration, where the boron atom adds to the less substituted carbon while hydrogen adds to the more substituted carbon. Propene reacts with borane to form tri-$n$-propylborane: $3\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{BH}_3 \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2)_3\text{B}$.

Oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide cleaves the boron-carbon bonds, replacing boron with hydroxyl groups: $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2)_3\text{B} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow 3\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Na}_3\text{BO}_3$.

The product is propan-1-ol, with the hydroxyl group on the terminal carbon. Tri-$n$-propylborane is an intermediate, tri-iso-propylborane would result from Markovnikov addition, and propan-2-ol forms through acid-catalyzed hydration.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

57800.subject: Chemistry
57800.text: The reaction of propane with bromine in presence of UV light predominantly forms
57800.sol:
The reaction between propane and bromine under UV light is a free radical substitution mechanism. The key selectivity arises during hydrogen abstraction, where bromine radicals target propane's six primary and two secondary hydrogens.

The secondary radical, $\mathrm{CH_3 CH\cdot CH_3 }$, is more stable than the primary radical due to hyperconjugation and inductive effects. Bromination is highly selective, favoring formation of the more stable radical with lower activation energy.

Thus, 2-bromopropane forms predominantly.

$\mathrm{CH_3 CH_2 CH_3 + Br\cdot \rightarrow CH_3 CH\cdot CH_3 + HBr}$

$\mathrm{CH_3 CH\cdot CH_3 + Br_2 \rightarrow CH_3 CHBrCH_3 + Br\cdot}$

The major product is 2-bromopropane.

60237.subject: Mathematics
60237.sol:
Finding the maximum of $f(x) = (1/x)^x$

Rewriting as $f(x) = x^{-x}$ and taking the natural logarithm gives $\ln y = -x \ln x$, where $y = f(x)$.

Differentiate both sides with respect to $x$, yielding:

$\frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx} = -(\ln x + 1) \quad \text{via product rule on} \quad -x \ln x$

$\frac{dy}{dx} = -y(\ln x + 1)$

Substitute $y = x^{-x}$ to obtain the derivative:

$\frac{dy}{dx} = -x^{-x}(\ln x + 1)$

Setting $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ for critical points, and noting $x^{-x} > 0$ for $x > 0$, solve:

$\ln x + 1 = 0 \quad \Rightarrow \quad \ln x = -1 \quad \Rightarrow \quad x = e^{-1}$

The first derivative test confirms a local maximum at $x = e^{-1}$: derivative is positive for $x < e^{-1}$ and negative for $x > e^{-1}$.

The maximum value is:

$f\left(\frac{1}{e}\right) = e^{1/e}$

Given the options, only $\mathrme^{\mathrm{e}}$ is a constant, while B, C, and D depend on $x$, suggesting a potential inconsistency with the calculated result $e^{1/e}$.

61427.text: General solution of the differential equation $\cos x(1+\cos y) \mathrm{d} x-\sin y(1+\sin x) \mathrm{d} y=0$ is
61427.sol:
Given differential equation is
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos x(1+\cos y) \mathrm{d} x-\sin y(1+\sin x) \mathrm{d} y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \cos x(1+\cos y) \mathrm{d} x=\sin y(1+\sin x) \mathrm{d} y \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x} \mathrm{ d} x=\frac{\sin y}{1+\cos y} \mathrm{ d} y
\end{aligned}$
Integrating on both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \int \frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x} \mathrm{ d} x=\frac{\sin y}{1+\cos y} \mathrm{ d} y+\log |\mathrm{c}| \\
& \Rightarrow \log |1+\sin x|=-\log |1+\cos y|+\log |\mathrm{c}| \\
& \Rightarrow \log |1+\sin x|+\log |1+\cos y|=\log |\mathrm{c}| \\
& \Rightarrow \log |(1+\sin x)(1+\cos y)|=\log |\mathrm{c}| \\
& \Rightarrow(1+\sin x)(1+\cos y)=\mathrm{c}
\end{aligned}$

Intersecting this with $L_1$ by substituting $y = -x$ yields $3x - (-x) - 1 = 0$, so 4x = 1 and $x = \frac{1}{4}$ with $y = -\frac{1}{4}$.

The distance between (1,2) and $\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)$ is found as $\sqrt{\left(\frac{-3}{4}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{-9}{4}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16} + \frac{81}{16}} = \sqrt{\frac{90}{16}} = \frac{3\sqrt{10}}{4}$.

Final answer: $\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{4}$ units.

Simplifying, $3 = 2 + 2 \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}$, so $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = \frac{1}{2}$. Using the dot product definition, $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = |\bar{a}||\bar{b}| \cos \theta = \cos \theta$. Thus, $\cos \theta = \frac{1}{2}$, yielding $\theta = rccos(\frac{1}{2}) = \frac{\pi}{3}$.

Resonant frequency analysis

The series combination of inductors $L$ and $2L$ yields equivalent inductance $L_{eq} = L + 2L = 3L$.

Substituting gives $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{9LC}} = \frac{1}{6\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.

66758.text: The magnetic potential energy stored in a certain inductor is $49\ \text{mJ}$ when the current in the inductor is $70\ \text{mA}$. The inductance of the inductor is
66758.sol:
The magnetic potential energy stored in an inductor is given by:

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} L I^2$

Rearranging for inductance $L$:

$L = \dfrac{2U}{I^2}$

Substituting the given values $U = 49 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{J}$ and $I = 70 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{A}$:

$L = \dfrac{2 \times 49 \times 10^{-3}}{(70 \times 10^{-3})^2}$

$L = \dfrac{98 \times 10^{-3}}{4900 \times 10^{-6}}$

$L = \dfrac{98 \times 10^{-3}}{4.9 \times 10^{-3}}$

$L = 20\ \text{H}$

Answer: $20\ \text{H}$

66777.text: The current flowing through the inductor of self inductance 'L' is continuously increasing at constant rate. The variation of induced e.m.f. (e) versus $\dfrac{dI}{dt}$ is shown graphically by figure
66777.sol:
The induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) in an inductor is given by Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, which incorporates Lenz's law:

$e = -L \dfrac{dI}{dt}$

Here, $e$ is the induced e.m.f., $L$ is the self-inductance of the coil, and $\dfrac{dI}{dt}$ is the rate of change of current.

Comparing this equation with the standard equation of a straight line passing through the origin, $y = mx$:
We have $y = e$ and $x = \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.
The slope of the line is $m = -L$.

Since the self-inductance $L$ is a positive constant, the slope $m$ is negative. Therefore, the graph of $e$ versus $\dfrac{dI}{dt}$ will be a straight line passing through the origin with a negative slope. As $\dfrac{dI}{dt}$ is positive (current is increasing), $e$ will be negative.

This linear relationship with a negative slope is correctly represented by the graph in figure C.

Answer: C

70134.subject: Physics
70134.text: In a single slit diffraction pattern, the distance between the plane of the slit and the screen is $1.4$ m. The width of the slit is $0.66$ mm. The second maximum is formed at the distance of $2.8$ mm from the center of the screen. The wavelength of light used is
70134.sol:
The position of the $n$-th secondary maximum in a single slit diffraction pattern is given by:

$y_n = \dfrac{(2n + 1)\lambda D}{2a}$

For the second maximum, $n = 2$:

$y_2 = \dfrac{5\lambda D}{2a}$

Rearranging for the wavelength $\lambda$:

$\lambda = \dfrac{2a y_2}{5D}$

Given values are:
$D = 1.4$ m
$a = 0.66$ mm $= 0.66 \times 10^{-3}$ m
$y_2 = 2.8$ mm $= 2.8 \times 10^{-3}$ m

Substituting the values into the formula:

$\lambda = \dfrac{2 \times 0.66 \times 10^{-3} \times 2.8 \times 10^{-3}}{5 \times 1.4}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{3.696 \times 10^{-6}}{7}$

$\lambda = 0.528 \times 10^{-6}$ m

$\lambda = 5280 \times 10^{-10}$ m $= 5280 \ \text{\AA}$

Answer: $5280 \ \text{Å}$

70175.text: In Young's double slit experiment, in an interference pattern second minimum is observed exactly in from of one slit. The distance between the two coherent sources is ' d ' and the distance between source and screen is 'D'. The wavelength of light source used is
70175.sol:
In Young's double-slit experiment with slit separation d and screen distance D, the path difference at position y is given by $\Delta x = \frac{yd}{D}$.

For the second minimum, the condition $\Delta x = \left(n - \frac{1}{2}\right)\lambda$ with $n=2$ yields $\Delta x = \frac{3}{2}\lambda$.

Since the minimum is observed exactly in front of one slit, set $y = \frac{d}{2}$ and equate the expressions: $\frac{(d/2)d}{D} = \frac{3}{2}\lambda$, which simplifies to $\frac{d^2}{2D} = \frac{3}{2}\lambda$.

Solving for $\lambda$ gives $\lambda = \frac{d^2}{3D}$, corresponding to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

70911.subject: Biology
70911.text: Which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the nervous system of Planaria?
options: It is the most primitive animal having CNS
It belongs to the phylum Aschelminthes.
The eyes are located on dorsal side of the brain
70911.sol:
Planaria belongs to the phylum Platyhelminthes, not Aschelminthes. It is a flatworm.

It is considered the most primitive animal to possess a central nervous system (CNS), which consists of a bilobed (often described as inverted U-shaped) brain and two longitudinal nerve cords connected by transverse nerves, forming a ladder-like structure.

The eyespots (ocelli) are located on the dorsal side of the head, near the brain, and are sensitive to light.

Therefore, the statement that it belongs to the phylum Aschelminthes is incorrect.

Answer: It belongs to the phylum Aschelminthes.

71209.subject: Biology
71209.text: The microbes which are used as biocontrol agents of pests include __________.
71209.sol:
Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests. The microbes used as biocontrol agents include bacteria, fungi, protozoans, and viruses.

Examples include:
Bacteria: Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control butterfly caterpillars.
Fungi: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi that are very common in the root ecosystems and are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens.
Viruses: Baculoviruses are pathogens that attack insects and other arthropods, widely used as species-specific, narrow spectrum insecticidal applications.
Protozoans: Nosema locustae is used to control grasshoppers and other insects.

Algae, lichens, viroids, and prions are not used as biocontrol agents.

Answer: bacteria, fungi, protozoans and viruses

71418.subject: Biology
71418.text: Which one of the following is the activator for enzyme hexokinase in glycolysis?
71418.sol:
Hexokinase is the first enzyme in the glycolysis pathway, which catalyzes the phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate using ATP.

The true substrate for hexokinase is not free ATP, but the $\text{Mg}^{++}$-ATP complex. The $\text{Mg}^{++}$ ion shields the negative charges of the phosphate groups in ATP, making the terminal phosphorus atom an easier target for nucleophilic attack by the hydroxyl group of glucose.

Therefore, $\text{Mg}^{++}$ acts as an essential cofactor and activator for the enzyme hexokinase.

Answer: $\text{Mg}^{++}$

71440.subject: Biology
71440.text: Identify the step, in which phosphorylation occurs with the help of inorganic phosphate and not ATP.
71440.sol:
In glycolysis, the conversion of Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate is catalyzed by the enzyme glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase.

During this step, oxidation of Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate occurs, and inorganic phosphate (H_3PO_4$ or $P_i$) is added to form 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate. ATP is not utilized in this phosphorylation step.

In the conversion of Glucose to Glucose-6-phosphate, ATP is used as the phosphate donor.

In the conversions of 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to 3-phosphoglycerate and Phosphoenol pyruvate to Pyruvic acid, ATP is synthesized (substrate-level phosphorylation).

Answer: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (3C) \rightarrow 1,3 bisphosphoglycerate (3C)$

71451.subject: Biology
71451.text: During aerobic respiration, the total number of ATP formed from one glucose molecule through substrate level phosphorylation is ----------------------.
71451.sol:
SIn aerobic respiration, ATP is synthesized from a single molecule of glucose through two distinct pathways: substrate-level phosphorylation and oxidative phosphorylation.

In the classical balance sheet of aerobic respiration, the complete oxidation of one glucose molecule yields a net total of $38$ ATP molecules. This total consists of $34$ ATP molecules produced via oxidative phosphorylation in the electron transport chain and $4$ ATP molecules produced via substrate-level phosphorylation.

The breakdown of ATP formed directly by substrate-level phosphorylation is as follows:

In glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm, a gross total of $4$ ATP molecules are synthesized during the payoff phase. However, $2$ ATP molecules are consumed during the initial preparatory phase, leaving a net gain of $2$ ATP molecules.

In the Krebs cycle, which takes place in the mitochondrial matrix, $1$ GTP molecule (equivalent to $1$ ATP) is generated directly per turn during the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate. Since one molecule of glucose gives rise to two molecules of acetyl-CoA, the Krebs cycle operates twice per glucose molecule, resulting in the production of $2$ ATP molecules.

Summing up the net contributions from both stages, the total number of net ATP molecules formed through substrate-level phosphorylation is:
$2\text{ (from glycolysis)} + 2\text{ (from Krebs cycle)} = 4\text{ ATP}$

Answer: $4$

72353.text: A convex lens of refractive index $\mu$ has two surfaces of equal radius of curvature $R$. The focal length of convex lens is
72353.sol:
Using the lens maker's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)

For a biconvex lens with equal radii of curvature, $ R_1 = +R$ and $R_2 = -R$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu -1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{2}{R} \right)

$ f = $\dfrac{R}{2(\mu - 1)}$$

Answer: $$\dfrac{R}{2(\mu - 1)}$

72615.subject: General Ability
72615.text:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Can agricultural productivity meet human needs in the long run? Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily. Global population growth, while showing signs of slowing down, has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture, accelerating worldwide ecological disruptions. Reserves of arable land and fresh water have diminished alarmingly. Chemical runoffs have compounded pollution problems. Invasion of natural habitats have hastened species extinction. Desertification has been severe in the last hundred years, especially in North Africa, southern portions of Africa, Australia, northern Mexico, and the American Southwest. Tropical forests have shrunk by one-half since World War II, with agricultural pressures causing three-quarters of that loss. Government intervention has produced its share of catastrophes, ranging from a terrible famine in China between 1958-1961 that may have killed 30 million people and destroyed the Aral Sea. Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.

What is the conclusion of the author in the passage about the prospects of agriculture in the world?
options: The author is both hopeful and sceptical of the prospects of agriculture
The author is very hopeful of the prospects of agriculture
The author is sceptical of the prospects of agriculture
The author is neither hopeful nor sceptical of the prospects of agriculture
72615.sol:
The concluding sentence of the passage states, "Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century."

This indicates that while the author retains some hope for the future of agriculture, the lack of optimism and the numerous challenges listed throughout the passage reflect a strong sense of scepticism. Thus, the author is both hopeful and sceptical about the prospects of agriculture.

Answer: The author is both hopeful and sceptical of the prospects of agriculture

73779.subject: General Ability
73779.text: An object is placed far beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The object then starts accelerating towards the mirror. Which one of the following is correct?
options: The image will accelerate towards the centre of curvature.
The image will accelerate towards the focus.
The image will accelerate towards the pole of the mirror.
The image will move with a constant speed towards the focus.
73779.sol:
Using the mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get the velocity of the image $v_i$ in terms of the velocity of the object $v_o$:

$-\dfrac{1}{v^2} \dfrac{dv}{dt} - \dfrac{1}{u^2} \dfrac{du}{dt} = 0$

$v_i = -\left(\dfrac{v}{u}\right)^2 v_o = -\dfrac{f^2}{(u-f)^2} v_o$

Since the object is moving towards the mirror, $u$ is increasing (becoming less negative), so $v_o > 0$. This makes $v_i < 0$, meaning the image moves in the negative direction (away from the mirror). For an object moving from $-\infty$ to the centre of curvature $C$, the image moves from the focus $F$ to $C$. Thus, the image moves towards the centre of curvature.

To find the acceleration of the image $a_i$, we differentiate $v_i$ with respect to $t$:

$a_i = \dfrac{dv_i}{dt} = -\dfrac{f^2}{(u-f)^2} a_o + \dfrac{2f^2}{(u-f)^3} v_o^2$

Here, $a_o > 0$ because the object is accelerating towards the mirror. Since the object is placed in front of the concave mirror, $u$ and $f$ are negative, and $|u| > |f|$, which means $(u-f) < 0$.

Therefore, both terms in the expression for $a_i$ are negative, yielding $a_i < 0$.

Since both the velocity $v_i$ and the acceleration $a_i$ of the image are negative, the speed of the image is increasing in the direction away from the mirror. Hence, the image accelerates towards the centre of curvature.

Answer: The image will accelerate towards the centre of curvature.

76755.text:
Given a function
$f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ccc}

$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x})=\left\{$\begin{array}{ccc}
-1 & , & $\mathrm{x}$ \leq 0 \\
$\mathrm{ax}+\mathrm{b}$ & , & 0 < $\mathrm{x}$ < 1 \\
1, & $\mathrm{x}$ \geq 1
\end{array}$\right. \\
& \text{ At } x=0 \text{, } \\
& \text{ L.H.L. = R.HL. } \\
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x) \\
& -1=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(a x+b) \\
& -1=b
\end{aligned}$
Since the given function is also continuous at x = 1
L.H.L. = R.H.L.
$\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}} f(x) \\ & a+b=1 \\ & a-1=1 \\ & a=1+1=2\end{aligned}$
Function is continuous at x = 0
$\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x) \\
& -1=a(0)+b \Rightarrow b=-1
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})$ is also continuous at $\mathrm{x}=1\begin{aligned}
& \lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1^{+}} f(x) \\
& a(1)+b=1 \\
& a=1-b=1+1 \\
& a=2 .
\end{aligned}$
b = –1.

77050.text: Let $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ be two solutions of the differential equation $\frac{d y}{d x}=x$. If $y_1(0)=0$ and $y_2(0)=4$, then what is the number of points of intersection of curves $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ ?

Given, D.E. $\frac{d y}{d x}=x\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \int d y & =\int x d x \\ \Rightarrow & y & =\frac{x^2}{2}+c\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad y_1(x)=\frac{x^2}{2}+c_1$ ...(i)
and $\quad y_2(x)=\frac{x^2}{2}+c_2$ ...(ii)
For $y_1(0)=0$ in equation (i)
$0=0+c_1\Rightarrow \quad c_1=0\Rightarrow \quad y_1(x)=\frac{x^2}{2} \quad$ ...(iii)
For $\quad y_2(0)=0\Rightarrow \quad 4=0+c_2 \quad[$ From (iii) $]$
For, $\quad c_2=4\Rightarrow \quad y_2(x)=\frac{x^2}{2}+4 \quad$ ...(iv)
For number of points of intersection for $y_1(x) and y_2(x)$ solving (iii) and (iv)
$\frac{x^2}{2}=\frac{x^2}{2}+4 \text{ (not possible) } 
as
$0 \neq 4$
Hence, no point of intersection.$

78443.subject: Mathematics
78443.text:
Paragraph: The interior angles of a polygon of n sides are in AP. The smallest angle is $120^{{}^{\circ}}$ and the common difference is $5^{{}^{\circ}}$.
Question: How many possible values can n have?
78443.sol:
Here, $a=120^{{}^{\circ}}$ and d=5.
Sum of angles of polygon $=(n-2) 180^{{}^{\circ}}\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{n}{2}[2 a+(n-1) d]=(n-2) 180 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{n}{2}[2 \times 120+(n-1) 5]=(n-2) 180 \\
& \Rightarrow n^2-25 n+144=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(n-9)(n-16)=0 \\
& \therefore n=9,16
\end{aligned}$
For $n=9, T_9=120+(9-1)^{5}=160$
For $n=16, T_{16}=120+(16-1)^{5}=195$ [not possible]

78501.subject: Mathematics
78501.text: If the AM and HM of two numbers are 27 and 12 respectively, then what is their GM equal to?
78501.sol:
Let the two numbers be $a and b$.
So, $\frac{a+b}{2}=27$, and
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}}{2}=12 \Rightarrow \frac{b+a}{2 a b}=12 \\
& \Rightarrow a b=\frac{27}{12}=\frac{9}{4} \\
& \therefore \text{ G.M. }=\sqrt{a b}=\frac{3}{2}
\end{aligned}$

78561.subject: Mathematics
78561.text:
For the set of numbers
$x, x, x+2, x+3, x+10$
where $x$ is a natural number, which of the following is/are correct?
1. Mean > Mode
2. Median > Mean
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
78561.sol:
Natural numbers : $x \cdot x, x+2, x+3, x+10$
Mode $=$ Most number of times repeated number
$\therefore$ Mode $=x\rightarrow$ Mean of the numbers,
$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Mean }=\frac{x+x+x+2+x+3+x+10}{5} \\
& \bar{x}=\frac{5 x+15}{5}=x+3
\end{aligned}$
Median of the numbers,
Numbers in ascending order :
$\begin{aligned}
& x, x, x+2, x+3, x+10 \\
& n=5 \text{ (i.e. odd numbers) } \\
& \mathrm{M}=\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)^{\text{th }} \text{ observation } \\
& =\left(\frac{5+1}{2}\right)^{\text{th }} \text{ observation }=3^{\text{rd }} \text{ observation } \\
& \therefore \mathrm{M}=x+2
\end{aligned}$
Hence, Mean > Median > Mode

81850.subject: Chemistry
81850.text:
Consider the following statements about the solutions formed by mixing two liquids.
A. An ideal solution thus formed obeys Raoult's law throughout the composition range.
B. Mixture of chloroform and acetone shows negative deviation from Raoult's law.
C. Mixture of aniline and phenol shows positive deviation from Raoult's law.
81850.sol:
Statement A is correct as an ideal solution is defined as one that obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration.

Statement B is correct because in a mixture of chloroform and acetone, intermolecular hydrogen bonding occurs between the two different molecules. This makes the A-B interactions stronger than the A-A and B-B interactions in the pure liquids, resulting in a lower vapour pressure and a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

Statement C is incorrect because a mixture of aniline and phenol also exhibits strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding between the phenolic proton and the lone pair on the nitrogen atom of aniline. This leads to stronger A-B interactions compared to the pure liquids, resulting in a negative deviation from Raoult's law, not a positive deviation.

Therefore, only statements A and B are correct.

Answer: A and B only

82500.sol:
The energy of light of wavelength $\lambda$ is given by

$\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{hv}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda} \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\mathrm{E}}$Here, $\mathrm{h}=$ Planck's constant $=6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J}-\mathrm{s}\mathrm{c}=$ speed of light $=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\mathrm{E}=$ energy gap $=1.9 \mathrm{eV}=1.9 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J}$
Substituting the given values in Eq. (i), we get

$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \quad \lambda$& =$\frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{1.9 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$\\
& =6.54 $\times$10^{-7} $\mathrm{~m} \approx$654 $\mathrm{~nm}
\end{aligned}$Thus, the wavelength of light emitted from LED will be $654 \mathrm{~nm}$.

If the radius of a star is $R$ and it acts as a black body, what would be the temperature of the star, in which the rate of energy production is $Q$ ?

So, the rate energy production
$\begin{aligned}
& Q=E \times A \\

\end{aligned}$
Temperature of star
$T=\left(\frac{Q}{4 \pi R^2 \sigma}\right)^{1 / 4}$

From the diagram,

$PM = 1 + {t}^{2}$
$PS = \sqrt{{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)}^{2} + 4{t}^{2}} = \left({t}^{2} + 1\right)$
$MS = \sqrt{4 + 4{t}^{2}} = 2\sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}}$
$⇒ 2\sqrt{1 + {t}^{2}} = 1 + {t}^{2}$
$∴ PM = 1 + {t}^{2} = 4 ⇒ {t}^{2} = 3$
$∴$ Area of $∆ PMS = \beta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\left({4}^{2}\right) = 4\sqrt{3}$ sq. units

Hence, ${\beta}^{2} = 48$

We have, $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{ \left({x}_{i} +1\right)}^{2} = 11n \ldots \ldots . \left(i\right)$
and $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{ \left({x}_{i} -1\right)}^{2} = 7n \ldots \left(ii\right)$
Adding $\left(i\right)$ and $\left($ ii\right)$ , we get

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_i^{2} + n = 9n ⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_i^{2} = 8n$
$⇒ \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_i^{2}}{n} =8$
Subtracting $\left($ i\right)$ and \left($ ii\right),$ we get
4\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i} = 4n ⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i} = n ⇒ \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i}}{n} =$$1$
Now, variance $= $$\dfrac{1}{n}$$\left[\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_ i^{2}\right] -$ {\$ left[\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i}}{n}\right]$}^{2} =8 - 1 = 7$

92187.text: Given four points A $\left(2, 1, 0\right), B \left(1, 2, 3\right), C \left(3, 1, 1\right)$ and $D\left(0, 1, 3\right)$. Point $D$ lies on the line $L$ which is perpendicular to the plane determined by the points A, B, C .$ If the point of intersection of the plane determined by the points A, B, C$ and the line $L$ is $\left(a, b, c\right)$, then $9\left(a + b + c\right) is equal to$
92187.sol:
Equation of the plane through $A, B, C$ is
$\left|\begin{cases}x - 2 & y - 1 & z - 0 \\ 1 - 2 & 2 - 1 & 3 - 0 \\ 3 - 2 & 1 - 1 & 1 - 0\end{cases}\right| = 0 ⇒ \left|\begin{cases}x - 2 & y - 1 & z \\ - 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$
$⇒ \left(x - 2\right)\left(1\right) - \left(y - 1\right)\left(- 4\right) + z\left(- 1\right) = 0$
$⇒ x - 2 + 4y - 4 - z = 0$
$⇒ x + 4y - z - 6 = 0$
Equation of the line through $D$ and perpendicular to the plane is
$\dfrac{x - 0}{1} = \dfrac{y - 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 3}{- 1}$
$∵$ Point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ is the point of intersection of the line and plane,

any general point on the line is $\left(\lambda, 4\lambda + 1, - \lambda + 3\right)$
It must satisfy the equation of the plane, so,
$\lambda + 16\lambda + 4 + \lambda - 3 - 6 = 0 ⇒ 18\lambda = 5$
$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{5}{18}$
Hence, $\left(a, b, c\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{5}{18}, \dfrac{38}{18}, \dfrac{49}{18}\right)$

$⇒ 9\left(a + b + c\right) = 46$

An ideal gas is enclosed in a vertical cylindrical container and supports a freely moving piston of mass $M$. The piston and the cylinder have an equal cross-sectional area $A$. Atmospheric pressure is ${p}_{0}$ and when the piston is in equilibrium, the volume of the gas is ${V}_{0}$. The piston is now displaced slightly from its equilibrium position. Assuming that the system, is completely isolated from, its surroundings, & what is the frequency of oscillation.
94147.sol:
& In equilibrium, pressure inside the cylinder = pressure just outside it

or & $\text{p} = {p}_{0} + \dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\text{A}}$

When piston is displaced slightly by an amount x, change in volume,

$\text{dV} = - \text{Ax}$

Since, the cylinder is isolated from the surroundings, nature of the process is adiabatic. In adiabatic process,

$\dfrac{\text{dp}}{\text{dV}} = - \gamma \dfrac{\text{p}}{\text{V}}$



or increase in pressure inside the cylinder,

$\text{dp} = - \dfrac{\left(\gamma \text{p}\right)}{\text{V}} \left(\text{dV}\right) = \gamma \left(\dfrac{{p}_{0} + \dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\text{A}}}{{V}_{0}}\right) \left(\text{Ax}\right)

This increase in pressure when multiplied with area of cross-section A will give a net upward force (or the restoring force). Hence,

\text{F} = - \left(\text{dp}\right) \text{A} = - \gamma \left(\dfrac{{p}_{0} A^{2} + \text{MgA}}{{V}_{0}}\right) \text{x}

Or \text{a} = \dfrac{\text{F}}{\text{M}} = - \gamma \left(\dfrac{{p}_{0} A^{2} + \text{MgA}}{{V}_{0} \text{M}}\right) \text{x}

Since, \text{a}$∝ - $\text{x}$,$ motion of the piston is simple harmonic in nature. Frequency of this oscillation is given by

\text{f} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left|\dfrac{\text{a}}{\text{x}}\right|} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma \left({p}_{0} A^{2} + \text{MgA}\right)}{{V}_{0} \text{M}}}$

100680.subject: Physics
100680.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a block on a rough horizontal surface pulled by a hanging mass via a string and pulley, if the horizontal surface is made completely smooth, the tension in the connecting string will decrease.
Reason (R): Removing friction increases the acceleration of the system, and for the hanging mass, the tension is given by $T = m_2(g - a)$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
100680.sol:
Let the mass of the block on the surface be $m_1$ and the hanging mass be $m_2$.

The equation of motion for the hanging mass is:
$m_2 g - T = m_2 a$
Rearranging this gives the tension in the string:
$T = m_2(g - a)$

When the horizontal surface is rough, there is an opposing frictional force $f_k$, and the acceleration is $a = \dfrac{m_2 g - f_k}{m_1 + m_2}$.

When the surface is made completely smooth, the opposing friction $f_k$ becomes zero. The net driving force on the system increases, which causes the acceleration $a$ of the system to increase.

Looking at the relation $T = m_2(g - a)$, as the acceleration $a$ increases, the term $(g - a)$ decreases. Consequently, the tension $T$ in the string decreases.

Therefore, both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason provides the correct physical explanation for the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

101172.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the radius of gyration ($k$) of various uniform symmetric bodies of radius $R$.

List-I (Body and Axis)List-II (Radius of Gyration)
A. Thin ring about its diameterI. $\dfrac{R}{2}$
B. Thin uniform disc about its diameterII. $\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$
C. Solid sphere about its diameterIII. $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R$
D. Hollow sphere about its diameterIV. $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R$

101172.sol:
The radius of gyration $k$ is given by $k = \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{M}}$.

A. For a thin ring about its diameter, $I = \dfrac{MR^2}{2} \implies k = \dfrac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$. (Matches II)

B. For a thin uniform disc about its diameter, $I = \dfrac{MR^2}{4} \implies k = \dfrac{R}{2}$. (Matches I)

C. For a solid sphere about its diameter, $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 \implies k = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R$. (Matches III)

D. For a hollow sphere about its diameter, $I = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^2 \implies k = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R$. (Matches IV)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

102421.subject: Physics
102421.text: Inside a stationary elevator, a simple pendulum has a time period $T_0$. In the same elevator, a projectile fired at a certain angle with a given initial speed has a time of flight equal to $T_0$. If the elevator now starts accelerating vertically upwards with an acceleration $a = g$ (where $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity), what will be the ratio of the new time period of the pendulum to the new time of flight of the projectile?
102421.sol:
In a stationary elevator, the effective gravity is $g$.

The time period of the simple pendulum is $T_p = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}} = T_0$.

The time of flight of the projectile is $T_f = \dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g} = T_0$.

When the elevator accelerates upwards with $a = g$, the effective acceleration due to gravity becomes $g_{\text{eff}} = g + a = 2g$.

The new time period of the pendulum is $T_p' = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{2g}} = \dfrac{T_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.

The new time of flight of the projectile is $T_f' = \dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{2g} = \dfrac{T_0}{2}$.

The ratio of the new time period to the new time of flight is:

$\dfrac{T_p'}{T_f'} = \dfrac{T_0 / \sqrt{2}}{T_0 / 2} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$.

The ratio is $\sqrt{2} : 1$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2} : 1$

104117.subject: Physics
104117.text: A coil draws a steady current of $2 \text{ A}$ when connected to a $100 \text{ V}$ d.c. source. When the same coil is connected to a $100 \text{ V}, 50 \text{ Hz}$ a.c. source, it draws an rms current of $1 \text{ A}$. The inductance of the coil is:
104117.sol:
For the DC source, the frequency is zero, so the inductive reactance $X_L = 0$. The coil acts as a pure resistor.
$R = \dfrac{V_{dc}}{I_{dc}} = \dfrac{100}{2} = 50 \, \Omega$

For the AC source, the coil offers both resistance and inductive reactance. The total impedance $Z$ is:
$Z = \dfrac{V_{ac}}{I_{ac}} = \dfrac{100}{1} = 100 \, \Omega$

The impedance of an RL circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$.
$100 = \sqrt{50^2 + X_L^2}$
$10000 = 2500 + X_L^2$
$X_L^2 = 7500 \implies X_L = 50\sqrt{3} \, \Omega$

The inductive reactance is $X_L = 2\pi f L$.
$50\sqrt{3} = 2\pi \times 50 \times L$
$50\sqrt{3} = 100\pi L$
$L = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}}{100\pi} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\pi} \text{ H}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\pi} \text{ H}$

104305.subject: Physics
104305.text:
Assertion (A): For an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum along the negative z-axis, if the electric field is along the positive x-axis, then the magnetic field must be along the positive y-axis.

Reason (R): The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the vector $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$, and the electric and magnetic fields are mutually perpendicular.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
104305.sol:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the cross product of the electric and magnetic field vectors, i.e., $\vec{v} \parallel \vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

Given that the wave propagates along the negative z-axis, the direction of propagation is $-\hat{k}$.

The electric field is along the positive x-axis, so $\vec{E}$ is along $+\hat{i}$.

We need to find the direction of $\vec{B}$ such that $\hat{i} \times \vec{B} = -\hat{k}$.

Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, it follows that $\hat{i} \times (-\hat{j}) = -\hat{k}$.

Therefore, the magnetic field must be along the negative y-axis ($-\hat{j}$).

The Assertion states that the magnetic field is along the positive y-axis, which is incorrect. The Reason correctly states the principle for finding the propagation direction. Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

104698.subject: Physics
104698.text:
A beam of unpolarized light is incident on a transparent glass surface from air. It is observed that the reflected beam is completely linearly polarized. If the angle of refraction in the glass is $30^{\circ}$, what is the speed of light in the glass medium?
(Given the speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$)
104698.sol:
When the reflected beam is completely linearly polarized, the light is incident at Brewster's angle ($i_p$).

At Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular. Therefore, the angle of incidence $i_p$ and the angle of refraction $r$ are related by:
$i_p + r = 90^{\circ}$

Given $r = 30^{\circ}$, we have:
$i_p = 90^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$

According to Brewster's law, the refractive index of the medium ($\mu$) is:
$\mu = \tan(i_p) = \tan(60^{\circ}) = \sqrt{3}$

The speed of light in the glass medium ($v$) is given by:
$v = \dfrac{c}{\mu} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $\sqrt{3} \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

106431.subject: Chemistry
106431.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The $2d$ subshell is not possible in any atom.
Reason (R): For a given principal quantum number $n$, the azimuthal quantum number $l$ can have values from $1$ to $n$ only.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
106431.sol:
Assertion (A) states that the $2d$ subshell is not possible. For a $d$ subshell, the azimuthal quantum number $l = 2$. If $n = 2$, the possible values for $l$ are $0$ and $1$. Since $l$ cannot be $2$ when $n = 2$, the $2d$ subshell does not exist. Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct.

Reason (R) states that $l$ can have values from $1$ to $n$. This is incorrect. According to quantum mechanical rules, for a given principal quantum number $n$, the azimuthal quantum number $l$ can have integer values ranging from $0$ to $(n-1)$. Therefore, Reason (R) is incorrect.

Hence, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

107727.subject: Chemistry
107727.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The carbon molecule ($\text{C}_2$) has a bond order of 2 and its double bond consists entirely of $\pi$-bonds.

Reason (R): In the molecular orbital configuration of $\text{C}_2$, the four valence electrons of the $2p$ subshell occupy the $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals, leaving the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital empty.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
107727.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. The $\text{C}_2$ molecule has 12 electrons. Its molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2$. The bond order is $\dfrac{8 - 4}{2} = 2$. Since the last four electrons enter the $\pi$ molecular orbitals, the double bond in $\text{C}_2$ consists of two $\pi$-bonds.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact explanation for (A). The fact that the four $2p$ electrons are accommodated in the degenerate $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals while the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital remains empty is the reason why the bond consists entirely of $\pi$-bonds.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

114379.subject: Chemistry
114379.text: The limiting molar conductivities of $\text{HCOONa}$, $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{NaCl}$ are $100$, $425$ and $125 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. If the molar conductivity of a $0.01 \text{ M}$ solution of $\text{HCOOH}$ is $40 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$, what is its degree of dissociation?
114379.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law, the limiting molar conductivity of $\text{HCOOH}$ is calculated from the strong electrolytes as follows:
$\Lambda^\circ_m(\text{HCOOH}) = \Lambda^\circ_m(\text{HCOONa}) + \Lambda^\circ_m(\text{HCl}) - \Lambda^\circ_m(\text{NaCl})$
$\Lambda^\circ_m(\text{HCOOH}) = 100 + 425 - 125 = 400 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

The degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) is given by the ratio of molar conductivity at a given concentration to the limiting molar conductivity:
$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda^\circ_m}$
$\alpha = \dfrac{40}{400} = 0.1$

Answer: $0.1$

116339.text:
Gas X is produced commercially by Deacon's process. When gas X reacts with dry slaked lime, it gives a compound Y which is widely used as a bleaching agent.

Transition metals act as effective catalysts because of their ability to change their oxidation states. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4 + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{V}_2\text{O}_5$

119303.subject: Chemistry
119303.text: The compound that CANNOT be obtained from the aldol condensation reaction shown below, is
119303.sol:
The given reaction is an aldol condensation between 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone and benzaldehyde in the presence of a base (NaOH) and heat.

First, we identify the possible enolates. 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone has only one enolizable $\alpha$-carbon (C5), as the other $\alpha$-carbon (C2) is blocked by two methyl groups. Thus, the enolate will form exclusively at the C5 position.

Next, we consider the possible condensation products:

1. Crossed Aldol Condensation: The enolate attacks the carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde. Subsequent dehydration (loss of water) forms a double bond between the C5 carbon of the cyclopentanone ring and the benzylic carbon. This yields an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone, 2-benzylidene-5,5-dimethylcyclopentanone. Both $E$ and $Z$ geometric isomers can be formed, which correspond to the structures in Option (1) and Option (3).

2. Self-Aldol Condensation: The enolate of 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone can also attack the carbonyl carbon of another molecule of 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone. The intermediate aldol addition product will have a hydroxyl group on the former carbonyl carbon of the electrophile.

For dehydration to occur under basic conditions (E1cB mechanism), an acidic $\alpha$-proton must be removed. The only available $\alpha$-proton is on the C5 carbon of the nucleophilic ring. Removal of this proton and the hydroxyl group leads to an exocyclic double bond, forming an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated system. This corresponds to the structure in Option (4).

Option (2) shows a product with an endocyclic double bond in the second ring. This is a $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated ketone. Forming this product would require the removal of a proton that is not $\alpha$ to any carbonyl group, which is not acidic enough to be removed by NaOH. Furthermore, aldol condensation is driven by the thermodynamic stability of the resulting conjugated $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated system.

Therefore, the unconjugated product in Option (2) cannot be obtained.

Answer:

122202.text: What type of skeleton do some cnidarians have?

122202.sol: Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic Cnidoblasts, also known as cnidocytes, contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture in cnidarians.They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Some of the cnidarians, e.g., corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa (Figure 4.6). The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. They have jointed appendages (arthros-joint,poda-appendages). Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system. Circulatory system is of open type. Sensory organs like antennae, eyes (compound and simple), statocysts or balancing organs are present. Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules. They are mostly dioecious. Fertilisation is usually internal. They are mostly oviparous. Development may be direct or indirect. Insects belong to the phylum Arthropoda, which is the largest phylum of Animalia and includes over two-thirds of all named species on earth.The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton. Sister chromatids have separated and are moving towards opposite poles of the cell.
Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids held together by a centromere and is aligned at the equatorial plate.
Chromosomal material appears as intertwined threads within an intact nuclear envelope.
123887.sol:
The stage most suitable to study the morphology of chromosomes is mitotic metaphase, because by this stage the condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be observed clearly under the microscope.

During mitotic metaphase, each chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids held together by a centromere. These chromosomes are moved to the spindle equator and get aligned along the metaphase plate.

The other options describe different stages of cell division: aligning as bivalents occurs in metaphase I of meiosis, separation of sister chromatids occurs in anaphase, and intertwined threads within an intact nuclear envelope are characteristic of prophase.

Answer: Each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids held together by a centromere and is aligned at the equatorial plate.

123895.text: Read the following statements regarding the substages of prophase I in meiosis and select the incorrect statement.
options: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis.

The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.
Diakinesis is marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata and represents transition to metaphase.
